# Build: urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve

## Brett said (verbatim)
> The approve and deny dialogue is still saying open, and I received the alarm, so it's still stopping.

## What to build
Continue build "URGENT: AmberX veto notice alarm too loud + Approve must go straight through" (urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"The approve and deny dialogue is still saying open, and I received the alarm, so it's still stopping."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Brett still gets an alarm/long vibration from the AmberX phone app on every axHub veto hold (it fires again with ~30 s left). axHub's ntfy push is already normal priority (hub hotfix ee5706f), so this comes from the AmberX app's own approval notice. Fix in AmberX: one normal notification per hold, no alarm channel, no repeat at 30 s; a settings switch per notification type (sound, vibration, alarm, repeat) in the AmberX notification panel. Also: the console approval dialog's Approve/Deny must act directly and close the dialog (no 'opened in axHub, approve or deny there'); see queued rebase of approve-button-fix and do it here if not done. Full API + voice control. Tests; report. Create its Plan Studio plan.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) The approve and deny dialogue is still saying open, and I received the alarm, so it's still stopping.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-3 for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

open: The console's owner sign-in fallback is only used when the browser's hub cookie doesn't arrive; it isn't set (`AXF_HUB_RELAY_USER` / `AXF_HUB_RELAY_PASSWORD` missing). With the hub's cookie domain `.amberxai.com`, a signed-in browser carries the cookie, so it should not be needed; if a tap still comes back with "no owner sign-in", the systems check item *Approvals relay* says what to set.
The Android channel change needs a new AmberX APK (CI builds it); the alarm is already off through the web config.
